documents.title: Immunization visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Lunch-hour appointment per PCP plan from his new patient visit. Shingrix #1 IM L deltoid. PCV20 IM R deltoid (indicated with his kidney condition). Told him the shingles shot can make him feel achy for a day or two. Second Shingrix due in 2 to 6 months, can be done at his physical in April. Tolerated, observed 15 min.

documents.title: Baby aspirin?
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, a coworker my age just started a baby aspirin and it got me thinking, with my dad's heart attack and my brother's stroke should I be on one too? I have my physical next month, happy to wait until then if that's easier. Thanks, Pat

documents.title: RE: Baby aspirin?
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good question and worth a real conversation rather than a quick yes or no. There are pros and cons for someone who hasn't had a heart attack or stroke himself. Let's go through it at the physical on the 23rd. No need to start anything before then.

medications.drug: aspirin 81 MG Delayed Release Oral Tablet

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
55 y/o M, annual exam. Feels well. No chest pain, no exertional symptoms, no dyspnea, no headaches, no urinary changes. Still seeing nephrology; he thinks his protein is "coming down" but no copies; their notes never arrived here despite two requests.

Meds lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40. NKDA.
Family: father MI 58, brother ischemic stroke 52, mother HTN/DM2.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Alert, well. Eyes, ears, throat normal. Thyroid not enlarged. No carotid bruits. Heart regular, no murmur or gallop. Lungs clear throughout. Abdomen soft, nontender, no masses. Trace edema at both ankles. Skin no lesions of concern. Normal gait.

Aspirin, from his portal question: talked through primary prevention at his age and family history. Benefit for someone without known vascular disease is small; GI bleeding and other bleeding risk is real and not trivial. He has no ulcer or bleeding history and is not on anything else that thins the blood. He would like to take it. Start aspirin 81 mg daily; stop and call with black stools or any bleeding. Revisit at a 6 wk check.

Prostate screening: discussed; he wants a PSA. Drawn today.

Other: lipids and CMP fasting next month (order in). Shingrix #2 today. Colonoscopy 2021 normal, next 2031. PHQ-2 0.

F/u ~6 weeks, BP and aspirin check.

documents.title: PSA result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Patrick, your PSA came back low and normal for your age. Nothing more needed on that for now. Remember the fasting labs at the end of May.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Six weeks into aspirin 81 for primary prevention. Takes it every morning with the lisinopril and statin, hasn't missed. No complaints at all: no stomach upset, no black stools, no nosebleeds or easy bruising.

BP 132/84, HR 78. BMI 27.
Fasting labs 5/29: TC 190, HDL 45, LDL 100, TG 225. Albumin still low, creatinine normal, as before.

No distress. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Trace ankle edema, unchanged.

A/P: Tolerating aspirin, continue. BP reasonable on lisinopril 20. Lipids reviewed with him; staying on atorvastatin 40. Back in the fall for BP, flu shot then.

documents.title: Clinical trial enrollment notice
documents.author: outside research center
documents.body:
To the primary care physician:

Your patient Patrick Michaud (DOB 02/21/1969) has consented to and enrolled in a randomized, double-blind study of an investigational antihypertensive agent given in addition to his usual blood pressure treatment. Neither the participant nor study staff know his assignment. Please continue his current medications, including lisinopril. Study visits include blood pressure checks and safety labs at our site.

Allergies on file with us: none known.

If he has a hospitalization or any new medication, we would be grateful for a call to the study coordinator at 413-555-0132. Unblinding for clinical need is available 24 hours a day through the same number.

Study coordinator, outside clinical research center

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Hypertension Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here for his BP check. Problems: hypertension, hyperlipidemia, membranous nephropathy (nephrology following).

Since August he is in a blinded trial of a new BP drug run by an outside research center; takes the study capsule along with his own lisinopril, atorvastatin and aspirin and says he hasn't missed doses. Has been watching salt, cooking more at home. Denies chest pain, breathlessness or lightheadedness.

BP 132/84. Other vitals flowsheet.
Exam: comfortable, heart and lungs normal, abdomen benign, no new findings.

Assessment/plan
- HTN: same reading as June; no change, the trial team is also checking him. Study medication noted (blinded).
- Membranous nephropathy: BMP and UA today for potassium and creatinine on the ACE inhibitor.
- Lipids: on atorvastatin 40.
- Flu and 2024-25 COVID vaccines given.
Next visit after the new year.

documents.title: Lab results from Wednesday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Potassium and kidney function are fine on the lisinopril. Urine still shows protein at the same level as last year, no blood. Nothing to change. Please let the trial team know these were drawn here in case they want copies.

documents.title: RE: Lab results from Wednesday
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Will do, thanks. Sore arm from the two shots but otherwise good.

documents.title: Refill - atorvastatin, lisinopril
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Mail-order pharmacy request, 90 days each of atorvastatin 40 and lisinopril 20. Seen 10/16, labs current. Sent per protocol, PCP cosign.
